sources.cite: Phelan EA, Mahoney JE, Voit JC, Stevens JA. Assessment and Management of Fall Risk in Primary Care Settings. Med Clin North Am 2015;99(2):281-293 (the CDC STEADI approach; author manuscript on CDC stacks)
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP case clinic-three-falls-five-new-pills, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes of the manuscript PDF: 'Postural hypotension is defined as a reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mm Hg or in diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing'; postural lightheadedness without a measured drop 'should be considered equivalent to postural hypotension for fall risk'; 'A key strategy is to reduce the dose of any indicated medications that contribute to fall risk and to taper and stop any medications that are no longer indicated'; for postural hypotension, reduce blood pressure-lowering drugs and stop drugs with it as a side effect; antidepressants, antipsychotics, sedative hypnotics, benzodiazepines, antihypertensives, NSAIDs and diuretics are linked to falls.
Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.
